research_spec.competing_explanation: If the added effect does not change ranking beyond variance, the earlier gap was about missing isolatable ablations rather than missing mechanism; any apparent benefit from richer descendants may come from backbone strength or regularization side-effects instead of the proposed support-removal stability signal.
expected_evidence: A matched control using the same encoder, optimizer family, sampler, and training budget but with the stability term disabled.
A mechanism-on/off comparison showing whether ranking changes when target-specific support masking and margin consistency training are active.
Per-user or per-item-sparsity slice NDCG@10 to test whether any effect concentrates where shortcut co-occurrence reliance should be strongest.
Training diagnostics for the auxiliary term magnitude and the fraction of batches where masked-support perturbations alter pairwise margins.
research_spec.falsifier: The proposal is falsified if the mechanism-on model fails to improve or consistently worsens full-sort NDCG@10 versus the exact matched control, or if the auxiliary loss remains inactive/degenerate so that masking support interactions produces no meaningful training-time margin constraint.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The wedge adds a new counterfactual training procedure: for each observed positive pair, it identifies historical support interactions within the user history, removes a sampled support interaction from the user-conditioned representation path, and explicitly regularizes the positive-vs-negative margin to remain stable. This introduces a mechanism-off switch unavailable in standard LightGCN/BPR variants and directly resolves the accepted gap by making the claimed effect isolatable and executable.
research_spec.hypothesis: The accepted context gap is that prior fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off. Under the frozen ML-1M full-sort protocol, a LightGCN descendant trained with target-support removal margin stabilization will provide that wedge: if brittle shortcut co-occurrence is truly a failure mode, then enforcing stable pairwise margins when sampled support interactions are removed should improve full-sort NDCG@10 over an exact matched control with the auxiliary path disabled; otherwise the mechanism should cleanly fail.
implementation_requirements: Add an auxiliary consistency loss that penalizes reduction of the original pairwise margin under support masking, with a static coefficient and no adaptive tuning.
Expose an exact mechanism-off condition by setting the auxiliary coefficient to zero and bypassing support masking while keeping all other code paths, data, and training budget identical.

For each training triple (u, i+, i-), compute a lightweight target-support attribution over the user's interacted items using similarity between the candidate positive embedding and historical item embeddings aggregated through the current user state.
Implement a LightGCN backbone with standard pairwise BPR scoring over the frozen train split.
Log auxiliary loss statistics and masking activity to verify the mechanism actually executes.
Retain protocol-compatible train-only fitting and full-sort evaluation without any held-out access during training.

Sample one or a small fixed number of high-support historical interactions for user u, construct a masked user representation with those interactions removed from the training-time aggregation path, and recompute the positive-negative margin.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the identical LightGCN backbone, embeddings, sampler, optimizer, epoch count, and evaluation pipeline, but disable support masking and set the consistency auxiliary coefficient to zero so the control reduces to ordinary pairwise LightGCN training.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Add a support-removal stability objective to LightGCN: alongside the standard BPR loss, the model estimates which user-history items most support each positive target, masks sampled support items from the user-conditioned aggregation path during training, and penalizes pairwise margin collapse between the original and masked states. The innovation is the explicit counterfactual mechanism-on/off wedge rather than a broader architecture rewrite.

research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come from extra parameters or stronger regularization rather than explicit exclusion modeling; the matched control must preserve parameter scale and optimization while removing only the exclusion channel and subtractive gate.
expected_evidence: Against a matched single-relation control with comparable embedding count, the dual-channel model changes ranking behavior most on users with broad or internally conflicting histories.
If the exclusion mechanism is real, its learned gate should activate more on candidate items that are close to sampled negatives or conflict-heavy neighborhoods than on straightforward positives.
Removing only the subtractive exclusion path while keeping the same attraction path and parameter budget should materially reduce any observed ranking advantage.
research_spec.falsifier: If a matched control that keeps the same backbone, parameter count, optimizer, and pairwise loss but disables the exclusion embeddings and subtractive gate matches or exceeds the proposed model on full-sort NDCG@10, then the hypothesized exclusion-memory wedge is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal directly addresses the accepted gap by introducing an explicit, isolatable mechanism-on/off wedge unavailable in the accepted frontier context: a second learned relation for user-conditioned exclusion plus a subtractive gate in scoring. It is a structural recommender change rather than a tuning variant because it adds a new latent relation, a new scoring decomposition, and a dedicated ablation path that can be cleanly disabled for diagnosis.
research_spec.hypothesis: Under the frozen ML1M full-sort pairwise protocol, a recommender that learns both attraction embeddings and user-conditioned exclusion embeddings, then scores each candidate with a disagreement-gated subtraction of exclusion evidence from attraction evidence, will improve ranking over a matched single-relation collaborative filtering control because repeated pairwise mistakes can become an explicit reusable negative preference signal; this provides the isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off missing in the accepted context.
implementation_requirements: Construct the matched control by keeping the same embedding dimensionality budget and optimizer but removing the exclusion channel and gate, reducing the score to the attraction component only.
Define score(u,i)=<u_attr,i_attr>-gate(u,i)*<u_excl,i_excl>, where gate is a bounded scalar derived from disagreement between attraction and exclusion channels for the same pair.
Implement a custom PyTorch recommender with user/item attraction embeddings and user/item exclusion embeddings under the recbole runtime training loop.
Keep the implementation within the allowed dependency set: python-stdlib, numpy, scipy, torch/pytorch, recbole-runtime.
Support full-sort prediction over all candidate items at evaluation time using only learned train-fit parameters.

Train with a pairwise ranking loss on positive-versus-sampled-negative items plus a light anti-collapse regularizer preventing attraction and exclusion embeddings from degenerating to the same direction.
Use standard pairwise BPR-style triples from the train split only; do not access held-out interactions during fitting or model selection.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the identical training pipeline, data split, pairwise sampler family, embedding budget, optimizer, and regularization schedule, but replace the dual-channel subtractive scorer with an attraction-only scorer so the only removed mechanism is explicit exclusion memory and its gate.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-relation collaborative filter with separate attraction and exclusion latent spaces and a disagreement-gated subtractive scorer, so negative evidence is represented as a first-class reusable user preference memory instead of being only implicit in pairwise updates.

causal_chain: Context shows accepted frontier and known-good packages were resource-deferred, while earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off.

If gains do not appear, or if a generic hard-negative variant matches them without the predicted popularity-specific pattern, then the diagnosis that popularity-shaped contrast is the missing mechanism is weakened.

If the comparison distribution is the active cause, the modified model should outperform the matched BPR-MF control specifically through better discrimination against exposed-but-unconsumed head items and improved recovery of preference-consistent alternatives in full-sort ranking.
In pairwise BPR-MF, many ranking errors can arise because uniformly sampled negatives are too easy and do not force separation from highly exposed but unconsumed items.
Replacing uniform negatives with popularity-conditioned negatives changes only the training comparison distribution while preserving backbone, scorer, and evaluation.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any difference versus BPR_MF is caused only by generic stochastic hardening from changing the negative sampler, not by the popularity-specific mechanism; therefore a popularity-conditioned sampler should not show a distinctive advantage over either the matched control or a generic mixed-negative alternative on the predicted slices.
discriminative_predictions: A generic hard-negative alternative such as mixed negatives may change training difficulty, but it should not reproduce the same popularity-specific slice pattern if popularity exposure is the operative cause.

Against the competing explanation, popularity-conditioned negatives should show larger relative gains than plain BPR_MF on users whose candidate lists are dominated by popular items, not merely a uniform lift across all users.
If the mechanism is real, the gain pattern should be more consistent on head-item suppression and tail-or-mid popularity recovery than would be expected from generic sampling noise.
expected_evidence: Full-sort NDCG@10 exceeds the matched BPR_MF control under the frozen split.
Score separation between observed positives and popular unobserved items increases relative to the control.
The mechanism-off ablation reverting to uniform negatives removes most of the effect if the sampler is causal.
User or item popularity-stratified analysis shows a stronger effect where popular distractors are more prevalent.
research_spec.falsifier: The proposal is falsified if popularity-conditioned negatives fail to improve over matched BPR_MF, or if a generic mixed-negative sampler matches or exceeds its effect without the predicted popularity-specific slice behavior.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This is intentionally a low-change, falsification-friendly wedge because the accepted context identifies the need for an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off rather than another composite mechanism. The change is restricted to the negative sampling operator so causal attribution is testable within the small qualification budget.
research_spec.hypothesis: BPR_MF with popularity-conditioned negative sampling will outperform matched BPR_MF on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 because training against exposure-plausible popular negatives teaches the model to reject attractive but non-preferred head items that uniform negative sampling under-trains against.
implementation_requirements: Implement or enable a popularity-proportional negative sampler over training items using only train interactions.
Keep the BPR-MF scorer, embedding dimensionality, optimizer family, and evaluation pipeline matched to the control.
Log popularity-stratified diagnostics for sampled negatives and ranked outputs to support falsification.
Provide an executable mechanism-off path that switches the sampler back to uniform negatives without altering any other training component.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched BPR_MF control with identical backbone, parameterization, optimizer schedule, train-only fitting, and full-sort evaluation; the only difference allowed is uniform negatives in the control versus popularity-conditioned negatives in the treatment.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Change the pairwise training sampler from uniform item negatives to popularity-conditioned negatives while leaving the BPR-MF scoring function unchanged.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism off = identical BPR_MF training and evaluation with the popularity-conditioned sampler disabled and replaced by the standard uniform negative sampler.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: A two-arm comparison between BPR_MF and BPR_MF__BPR_POPULARITY_NEGATIVE, with one additional diagnostic slice by user/item popularity, to test whether popularity-shaped negative exposure alone explains any ranking gain.
research_spec.observed_failure_mode: Accepted context reports that earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does popularity-conditioned negative sampling provide a causally attributable ranking benefit over matched BPR-MF, or are any apparent gains explainable by generic sampling difficulty alone?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: Because this proposal changes only the negative sampler on top of an already matched BPR_MF pipeline, it should fit within the existing qualification budget and is less resource-risky than deferred frontier composites.

causal_chain: A disagreement gate conditioned on the contrast between attraction and exclusion scores can suppress candidates that look broadly similar to positives but align with avoided patterns.
A standard single-relation scorer compresses both signals into one compatibility channel, so conflicting history can wash out specific dislikes or substitutions.
Separating attraction and exclusion embeddings creates two reusable user-item relations instead of one.
This should especially help ambiguous, substitute-heavy, and tail-consistent candidates, improving full-sort NDCG@10 under offline pairwise training.
Users often have historical neighborhoods containing both attraction evidence and implicit avoidance evidence.
research_spec.closest_parent: Explicitly learning a user-conditioned exclusion memory and subtractive gate alongside standard attraction embeddings will improve ranking quality because many hard negatives are not merely low-affinity items; they are items that align with patterns the user's history implicitly avoids.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain would come only from extra parameters or generic regularization, not from modeling an explicit exclusion relation.
discriminative_predictions: An ablation that removes the disagreement gate but keeps similar parameter count should lose most of the benefit if exclusion-aware routing, rather than capacity alone, is responsible.

Compared with a parameter-matched single-channel control, the proposed model should more often demote globally plausible but user-conflicting items while preserving or improving ranks for niche positives.

If the exclusion relation is the operative mechanism, improvement should be larger for users whose recent or overall histories induce high internal score conflict between attraction and exclusion channels than for low-conflict users.
expected_evidence: A measurable subset of top-ranked items whose final scores are reduced primarily by the exclusion channel, with these corrections correlating with ranking improvements.
Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than a matched BPR_MF control under the frozen split.
Stronger relative gains on users with diverse or substitute-heavy interaction histories.
research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched single-channel model and a no-gate ablation match or exceed the proposed model, especially without any concentration of gains on high-conflict users, the explicit exclusion-relation hypothesis is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the scorer from a single affinity relation to a dual-relation attraction-versus-exclusion mechanism with user-conditioned disagreement routing. That is a core representational and interaction change, not a tuning variant or thin wrapper on an existing listed profile.
research_spec.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that learns both attraction embeddings and exclusion embeddings, then scores each candidate through a user-conditioned disagreement gate between these two relations, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-channel collaborative filtering because it can explicitly suppress user-specific false positives created by mixed tastes and substitution structure.
implementation_requirements: Construct user attraction state from historical positives with simple train-time aggregation compatible with train-only fitting.
Construct user exclusion state from sampled negative contrast accumulated through the pairwise objective, without using held-out interactions.
Implement a PyTorch recommender with user/item attraction embeddings and user/item exclusion embeddings.
Provide ablations: no exclusion channel and no disagreement gate.
Score candidates as direct attraction score minus gated exclusion score, where the gate is a bounded function of attraction-exclusion disagreement.
Support full-sort ranking over all items at evaluation time within the protocol.
Train with a pairwise BPR-style loss on the final score plus light norm regularization.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched BPR_MF control with the same dataset split, optimizer family, training budget, embedding dimensionality scale, and pairwise evaluation protocol, differing only by the absence of the exclusion channel and disagreement gate.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce an explicit second latent relation for user-conditioned exclusion and a disagreement gate that modulates subtractive scoring between attraction and exclusion evidence.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Disable the exclusion channel by tying exclusion embeddings to zero and fixing the disagreement gate to zero, reducing scoring to a standard single-channel attraction model trained with the same pairwise loss.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: BPR-style matrix factorization extended with separate exclusion embeddings for users and items plus a scalar disagreement gate computed from attraction and exclusion score contrast; compare against matched BPR_MF and a no-gate ablation.
research_spec.research_question: Does explicitly modeling a user-conditioned exclusion relation, alongside attraction, improve offline full-sort Top-N recommendation under pairwise training beyond what matched single-channel collaborative filtering can achieve?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The minimal wedge is lightweight relative to graph models: two embedding tables per side and a small gating function should fit within the stated implementation ceiling and qualify within the 10 GPU minute / 30 wall minute budget on ML-1M-scale pairwise training.
